product.problem_statement: Traditional MDR services are rigid and passive, ultimately placing a heavy burden on internal enterprise teams. Moreover, standalone AI-based tools create additional management overhead. Companies have to cobble together multiple vendors, reducing operational efficiency.
product.solution: A hybrid model in which AI automates routine detection and response tasks, while human engineers take responsibility for complex decisions requiring judgment. All context (endpoints, cloud, SaaS, AI usage, etc.) is integrated and analyzed on a single platform (Aura).
key_features: AI agents detect threats within seconds and respond/isolate within minutes
Aura platform allows querying security environments in natural language
AI agents customized to each customer's environment
Detection of AI-specific threats such as prompt injection and dangerous MCP
Flexible service models: fully managed, co-managed, or engineer dispatch

product.target_customer: Fortune 500 enterprises and AI-native companies (e.g., Lovable, LastPass, Rogo, dLocal, Miro). Companies of all sizes that struggle to attract and retain security talent.

product.summary: SE3 is AI software that fuses sensor data from multiple manufacturers' drones, unmanned ground vehicles, etc., to create a single 3D battlefield map and enables commanding swarms via voice commands.

product.solution: SE3 processes sensor data from cameras, LiDAR, etc. using classical computer vision algorithms to build 3D spatial understanding, and layers an LLM (replaceable with customer-desired models) on top for natural language swarm operations. All processing performed on-edge, fully offline operation

motif-technologies-2026.tagline: An AI research lab building foundation models for AI agents from scratch.

founders.background: Holds a PhD in pure mathematics (arithmetic geometry) from Oxford University. Later pivoted to data science, working as a data scientist at Samsung Research and PUBG, and served as AI Director at AI infrastructure company Moreh, leading the development of the AMD GPU-based MoMo-70B model.
founders.notable_achievement: Invented a proprietary GDA (Groupwise Differential Attention) architecture, completing the 314B-parameter MoE model Motif 3 in five months with a team of 30.

motif-technologies-2026.team_highlights: Established in February 2025 as a spin-off from Moreh. Started with just over 10 people; now, about 30 employees, of which 25 are developers. The team combines Moreh's GPU cluster optimization technology with AI model design capabilities, taking a full-stack approach that handles everything from hardware infrastructure and kernels to model design and serving in-house.

product.summary: Motif Technologies develops foundation models for building AI agents that perform complex tasks. Its flagship model, Motif 3, is a Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture with 314 billion total parameters, activating only approx. 13.2 billion parameters during inference for efficiency. It is released open-weight under the MIT license and scored 47 on the global AI evaluation index AAII (Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index), the highest among models from countries outside the U.S. and China.
product.problem_statement: The global AI market is dominated by U.S. big tech companies like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic, as well as China's DeepSeek. Most Korean companies rely on fine-tuning foreign open-source models (e.g., Llama), which is seen as a weakness in terms of technological sovereignty and long-term competitiveness. Additionally, there is a shortage of models optimized for the new computing paradigm of AI agents.
product.solution: Applies its proprietary GDA (Groupwise Differential Attention) technology, an improvement on the attention mechanism of the Transformer architecture, to allocate more computational resources to key information in language and less to 'noise,' boosting efficiency. All components—from architecture design to tokenizer, optimizer, and kernel—are developed in-house with no external dependencies.
key_features: 314B-parameter Sparse MoE architecture (13.2B active during inference) for efficient inference
MIT-licensed open-weight for free download, distribution, and modification
Performance on par with global big tech models in agent and coding domains (AAII 47, #1 among non-U.S./China countries)
Pre-training completed in five months on 768 NVIDIA B200 GPUs
Expanding into a multimodal model covering text, image, and video
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The core technology is its proprietary GDA (Groupwise Differential Attention) architecture. It modifies standard Transformer attention to distinguish between core information and less important content in language, allocating computational resources differentially. The company also designed a proprietary Sparse MoE structure with 384 routed experts and one shared expert per MoE layer. The model comprises 53 layers: the first two are dense, and the remaining 51 are MoE layers.
product.target_customer: Global developers and enterprise customers. Key customers include companies that want to run open-weight models on their own infrastructure, startups needing models specialized for coding and AI agent workloads, and public institutions involved in government sovereign AI projects.
product.business_model: Currently preparing B2B licensing and cloud-hosted API services. Motif 3 has been listed on Microsoft Azure Marketplace, and plans to launch full-scale global API services after the release of Motif 4. Also provides domain-specific enterprise AI transformation (AX) solutions for finance, manufacturing, and public sectors. The long-term goal is to position as a replacement for in-house systems through low-cost enterprise pricing plans.

direct_competitors.comparison: Like us, a dedicated team building a proprietary AI foundation model. Develops the Solar Open2 (250B-A15B) LLM and document AI solutions. Competes with a strength in long-document processing with a 1M-token context window, and is ahead in funding with a Series C round.

direct_competitors.name: DeepSeek (China)
direct_competitors.comparison: A leading Chinese open-weight MoE model developer. Its V4 Pro scores in a similar range on AAII, competing at the top of the open-source landscape. Has significant advantages in capital and talent scale.

direct_competitors.name: Mistral AI (France)
direct_competitors.comparison: Europe's leading open-weight LLM developer, releasing models specialized for agents and coding. Leads in brand recognition and global partnerships but does not directly compete with Motif in the Korean market.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: A 'pure in-house design' philosophy: building everything from scratch without adapting external open-source architectures (e.g., Llama). The only company in South Korea developing both LLMs and large multimodal models (LMMs) in-house, and holds a unique attention structure called GDA. The ability of a small 30-person team to deliver performance on par with global big tech is also a key differentiator.
competitive_landscape.moat: Design know-how and patents for the proprietary GDA architecture, plus GPU optimization technology, form the core barriers. Training a 314B model with 768 GPUs in five months demonstrates that a small team can competitively develop large-scale models. Government support networks secured through participation in the sovereign AI project and a GPU infrastructure of 1,000 units are also intangible assets.

product.summary: MotifDrive develops 'MD-1,' an end-to-end autonomous driving software platform based on VLM that covers 360 degrees with only six cameras, without LiDAR or HD maps. product.problem_statement: Traditional ADAS uses a rule-based approach where humans manually code rules, making it difficult to handle edge cases like hand signals at construction zones or abnormally stopped vehicles. product.solution: A dual-loop architecture where an E2E neural network integrates perception, prediction, path planning, and control using only camera images, and a VLM supplements decision-making by understanding exceptional situations at a language level. The fast loop (E2E) ensures real-time performance, the slow loop (VLAM) handles contextual reasoning, and a Fail-Safety Layer double-checks both decisions.
key_features: Camera-only 6-unit configuration (front×2, side×2, rear×2) — 360° coverage
VLM-based integrated neural network — perception, prediction, path planning unified architecture
Dual-loop structure: E2E Fast Loop (real-time) + VLM/VLAM Slow Loop (contextual reasoning)
Double verification via Fail-Safety Layer
No need for expensive LiDAR or HD maps → lower BOM cost
Lightweight model optimized for automotive SoC (embedded)

The fast loop and slow loop operate at different frequencies and exchange information, achieving both real-time responsiveness (milliseconds) and high-level situational understanding (language reasoning). Unexpected situations that are hard to collect are reproduced and trained/validated in a World Model-based virtual environment.

product.summary: COSMOS LAB develops aqueous zinc-halogen batteries that use water as an electrolyte and are non-flammable. It achieves a cell-level energy density of approx. 170Wh/kg and has demonstrated 100% non-flammability.
product.problem_statement: Lithium-ion batteries carry a constant risk of thermal runaway fires in ESS and data centers. Additionally, there are supply chain risks and price volatility for key minerals such as lithium and cobalt. Conventional aqueous batteries have low energy density, and flow batteries increase system volume and cost due to external tanks and pumps.
product.solution: An aqueous battery with an integrated cell structure using a water-based non-flammable electrolyte and zinc-halogen materials. It eliminates external tanks and pumps and implements a prismatic form factor compatible with lithium-ion batteries. The 'Halogen Complete Fixation System' prevents halogen migration and loss, ensuring both lifespan and safety.
key_features: 100% non-flammable (water-based electrolyte, utilizing bromine-based halogen combustion suppression properties)
170Wh/kg cell energy density (based on 50Ah prismatic form factor)

Fully compatible with lithium-ion ESS infrastructure (standard prismatic form factor)

1,000 cycle lifespan (verified for 15Ah grade)
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: All elements—cathode, anode, separator, electrolyte, current collector, charge-discharge operation technology, cell structure, and manufacturing process—are self-developed and internalized. The 'Halogen Complete Fixation System' prevents halogen loss and optimizes the balance between density, safety, and lifespan. It has demonstrated the world's first standard 50Ah prismatic form factor and 170Wh/kg simultaneously in an aqueous battery.

In the mid- to long-term, expands applications to renewable energy-linked ESS, industrial power storage, and distributed grid markets.

product.summary: Volantis is developing an AI inference accelerator, the A-1. By using a photonic interposer (optical interconnect), it eliminates the trade-off between memory capacity and bandwidth. It is designed to infer models with over 20 trillion parameters at 10,000 tokens per second per user.
product.problem_statement: Real-time inference of ultra-large AI models (10 trillion+ parameters) requires enormous memory capacity and bandwidth simultaneously. Existing GPUs have fast SRAM bandwidth but limited capacity, while HBM offers large capacity but insufficient bandwidth. This 'memory wall' is the core bottleneck for AI inference speed and model size.
product.solution: Volantis developed 'photonic wires'—optical waveguides integrated into the interposer—to replace electrical traces connecting chips and memory. Optical signals can travel roughly 100 times farther than electrical signals without loss, so memory can be placed several centimeters away instead of directly next to the chip. This enables the A-1 to deliver up to 10TB of memory and 240TB/s bandwidth in a single package.
key_features: Chip-to-memory interconnect based on a photonic interposer
Integrated micro VCSELs (vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers); no external laser required
Targets less than 1 picojoule/bit power consumption per link
Target system power of 20kW
Heterogeneous packaging combining licensed IP (processor cores, HBM, etc.)
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Unlike existing silicon photonics approaches (e.g., Lightmatter, Celestial AI) that use external lasers and silicon photonic modulators, Volantis integrates gallium arsenide (GaAs)-based micro VCSELs directly into the interposer. The company claims this leverages the existing VCSEL supply chain, avoids indium phosphide (InP) supply risks, and offers advantages in temperature stability and cost.
product.business_model: Plans to generate revenue by selling the finished AI accelerator (A-1) or through subscription-based AI inference-as-a-service. For now, the priority is shipping its own chip rather than IP licensing.
product.target_customer: AI labs operating ultra-large models (10T–20T+ parameters), hyperscale cloud providers, and large-scale coding agent companies, among other enterprises that require real-time, high-performance inference.

direct_competitors.comparison: Develops silicon photonics-based AI accelerators and IP. Similar to Volantis, it uses optical interconnects but relies on external lasers and has IP licensing as its main business model.

direct_competitors.name: Celestial AI (acquired by Marvell)
direct_competitors.comparison: It first introduced the concept of HBM-at-a-distance via a photonic interposer, but was acquired by Marvell around 2025–2026 for approximately $5.5B. The technical direction is similar to Volantis, but Volantis differentiates by aiming to ship its own chip rather than IP licensing.

direct_competitors.name: NVIDIA
direct_competitors.comparison: The dominant player in the AI accelerator market. It is reportedly considering optical interconnects for its next-generation GPUs (post-Grace), but Volantis differentiates by tackling extreme scale (10TB memory) with a photonic interposer.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: It applies the photonic interposer exclusively to its own chip, creating a finished AI inference accelerator that delivers extreme memory capacity (10TB) and bandwidth (240TB/s) simultaneously. This contrasts with competitors that mostly focus on IP licensing.
competitive_landscape.moat: The founding team's experience directly developing core technologies such as HBM, CoWoS, and high-speed VCSELs is the biggest barrier to entry. In particular, Roy Meade (CTO, creator of HBM) and Inderjit Singh (developed the first CoWoS product) give the company an unrivaled position in packaging technology.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Still pre-silicon tapeout, with technical feasibility being the biggest risk. However, the team includes world-class memory/packaging experts, and investments from key AI figures such as Sam Altman and Jeff Dean have earned it high credibility.

It has emerged as a potential solver of the 'memory wall' in the AI semiconductor industry, and backing from prominent investors like Sam Altman also made headlines.

Angel investments from high-profile figures including Sam Altman, Jeff Dean, and John Doerr

Volantis's SAM is the inference accelerator market for ultra-large models (1 trillion+ parameters), estimated at tens of billions of dollars.

product.solution: Reach uses APIs from the security products a company already owns to collect real-time configuration data, analyzes it with AI models to identify misconfigurations or disabled features, then integrates with ticketing systems to automatically fix issues or activate compensating controls—blocking attack paths without requiring patches.
key_features: Blind spot identification: finds unconfigured, incomplete, or unused controls in existing security product settings.

Guided remediation: validates changes in a staging environment before deploying them via the ticketing system.
Continuous verification: monitors for drift after configuration changes and continuously verifies protection status.
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Uses domain-specific AI to understand the context of security control configurations. Provides real-time control status data to other AI systems or workflows via Reach’s API and MCP (Model Context Protocol) server.

product.business_model: SaaS subscription model. Pricing is estimated to be based on the number of security products and the scale of assets under control.

product.summary: Rise Reforming has developed a modular process that converts stranded biogas (methane + CO2) from wastewater treatment plants, farms, and landfills into high-value chemicals like dimethyl ether (DME), methanol, and dimethyl carbonate (DMC) on-site. Their proprietary 'bi-reforming' process (patent pending) integrates three steps—biogas purification, syngas production, and syngas upgrading—into a single container-sized system. They have validated stable syngas production for over 1,800 hours, and plan to launch the first biogas-to-methanol pilot in the Americas at a Chicago-area wastewater treatment plant in early 2027.
product.problem_statement: The U.S. chemical industry is centralized and fossil-fuel-dependent, making it vulnerable to geopolitical crises and natural disasters. At the same time, 60% of biogas produced in the U.S. is wasted in low-margin uses or flared. This biogas could be used to produce $20 billion worth of chemicals annually, but most of it is currently discarded.
product.solution: Rise Reforming captures wasted biogas on-site with modular equipment and converts it into high-value chemicals like DME, methanol, and DMC. The system is the size of one container, quick to install, easy to permit, and has the lowest feedstock cost. Scaling up is easy by adding more modules. The final products are price-competitive with fossil-fuel-based counterparts while having extremely low carbon emissions.
key_features: Container-sized modular design for easy on-site deployment and scaling
Integrated three-step process: biogas purification → bi-reforming → syngas upgrading (patent pending)
Can recover various byproducts: heat, electricity, chemicals
Low-carbon throughout: no need for fossil fuel feedstock or transportation
Can produce DME, methanol, DMC (high scalability with syngas derivatives)
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The core technology is the bi-reforming process that reacts biogas (CH4+CO2) with steam to produce syngas (H2+CO). It improves catalyst lifespan and efficiency compared to conventional reforming processes, and has demonstrated stable operation for over 1,800 hours. The syngas is then converted into DME and methanol via catalytic reactions.
product.target_customer: Initial targets: wastewater treatment plants and dairy farms (biogas suppliers) → DME offtakers (aerosol propellants, propane blend fuel) and methanol buyers (marine fuel, chemical feedstock). Long-term: landfills and large-scale biogas operators.
product.business_model: Pay the biogas producer a feedstock fee, install the module on their site, then sell the produced chemicals to industrial customers. Secure revenue stability through DME and methanol offtake agreements. Scale by adding modules; asset-light model with low fixed costs.

direct_competitors.comparison: LanzaTech converts industrial off-gases (CO, CO2) into ethanol via fermentation, but Rise Reforming directly reforms biogas to DME and methanol, and is more distributed with on-site modular units.
Velocys converts natural gas into liquid fuels via Fischer-Tropsch, but is focused on large-scale plants and not specifically on biogas.
